questions.question_text: Which decimal and percentage are equivalent to a probability of $\frac{3}{5}$?

options.why: Read the numerator and denominator as decimal digits instead of dividing.
Converted the complementary probability two-fifths instead of three-fifths.

questions.question_text: Which fraction and decimal are equivalent to a $10\%$ chance?

options.why: Moved the decimal point one place too far when converting ten percent.
Used the complementary ninety-percent chance instead of ten percent.

questions.question_text: Which benchmark word best describes an event with probability $0.7$?

options.why: Treated any probability below one as unlikely instead of comparing with one-half.
Treated a high probability as certainty even though it is less than one.

questions.question_text: Which list orders the probabilities $0.2$, $50\%$ and $\frac{4}{5}$ from least to greatest?

options.why: Ordered the values from greatest to least instead of least to greatest.
Compared the printed numbers without converting fifty percent to zero-point-five.

questions.question_text: A probability lies halfway between $0$ and $0.5$. Which set gives that point in equivalent forms?

options.why: Selected the upper endpoint instead of the midpoint between the benchmarks.
Divided one by five from seeing 0.5 instead of finding the midpoint.

questions.question_text: A forecast gives a $30\%$ chance of wind and a $\frac{2}{5}$ chance of rain. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Rain is more likely by $10$ percentage points.
Wind is more likely by $10$ percentage points.
options.why: Converts $\frac{2}{5}$ to $40\%$ correctly but names the smaller probability as the more likely one, reversing the comparison.

options.text: Wind is more likely by $5$ percentage points.
options.why: Matches $\frac{2}{5}$ to the wrong benchmark, treating it as a quarter and so reading it as $25\%$, then computing $30\% - 25\% = 5$ percentage points.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{2}{5}=40\%$
$40\%-30\%=10$ percentage points
Rain is more likely.
